definition: A research approach studying whether a stronger AI model can be effectively supervised and aligned using labels or feedback generated by a weaker model or weaker human oversight.
details: Weak-to-strong generalization research is motivated by the anticipated future challenge of humans needing to oversee AI systems that may exceed human capability in many domains, testing whether alignment techniques still work under this asymmetry.

explainer.lead: Weak-to-strong generalization studies whether a stronger AI model can be effectively supervised and aligned using labels or feedback from a weaker model or weaker human oversight. It matters because humans will need to oversee AI systems that may exceed human capability in many domains.

tiers.eli5: It asks whether a weaker teacher can still successfully guide a much smarter student.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers test whether alignment techniques still work when supervision is weaker than the model being supervised. The core question is whether the stronger model generalizes beyond its weak labels.
tiers.paperLevel: A research approach testing whether alignment techniques still work under the asymmetry where supervision comes from a weaker model or weaker human oversight.

explainer.example: A small model labels examples used to train a larger model, and researchers check whether the larger model is aligned despite the weaker feedback.

citation.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
